title: 8. Numeracy & Number Systems: Rounding Whole Numbers to a Given Place
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.concept: Rounding Whole Numbers to a Given Place
questions.learningObjective: Round a two-digit whole number to the nearest ten.
questions.question: Round \(47\) to the nearest ten.
questions.explanation: To round \(47\) to the nearest ten, look at the ones digit. The ones digit is \(7\). Since \(7\) is at least \(5\), round up. The tens digit increases from \(4\) to \(5\), and the ones digit becomes \(0\). Therefore, \(47\) rounded to the nearest ten is \(50\).
questions.hint: Look at the digit to the right of the place you are rounding to.

questions.concept: Rounding Whole Numbers to a Given Place
questions.learningObjective: Round a two-digit whole number to the nearest ten.
questions.question: Round \(63\) to the nearest ten.
questions.explanation: To round \(63\) to the nearest ten, look at the ones digit. The ones digit is \(3\). Since \(3\) is less than \(5\), keep the tens digit the same and change the ones digit to \(0\). Therefore, \(63\) rounded to the nearest ten is \(60\).
questions.hint: Look at the ones digit and decide: is it less than \(5\), or is it \(5\) or more?

questions.hint: Look at the tens digit when rounding to the nearest hundred.
